- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is mixed; add 1–3% to initial forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–4% to account for potential reversal or policy-driven support.
